On 8/10/13 1:16 PM, Martin ï¿½mï¿½ra wrote:
> Since I started with asking... Seems that I canï¿½t stop anymore :) Hope you donï¿½t mind...

>
> 1) Why do I get wierd distributions when i set wamup on low values (<20)?

Adaptation needs to find the appropriate scales (and optionally
covariance) of the parameters in order to sample efficiently.
When you don't warmup enough, the sampler tends not to be able to
move efficiently through the posterior.

>
> 2) Why do I get following error (and stop) everytime I try tu run with cppo_set="debug"?

No idea. Maybe one of the R gurus will know. Windows sometimes
have problems with different optimization levels because their
C++ compilers and linkers aren't as robust and tend to use more
memory.

> 4) Is there some easy way how to find out if my initial values were really accepted?

I'm not sure what you mean by accepted. If they are illegal,
you'll get a warning and sampling will stop (or maybe that's
only in 2.0 --- it's been so long since the last release I'm not
sure).
> I'm not sure sometimes.

But if we don't have the warning in place, you'll probably still
get a failure to initialize stepsize warning.

> And since
> there allways have to be some warmup, I can't check it. Can you check it please below? For case of multiple chains:

You can also use the test gradients operation.

> /myinits="function() {/
>
> /list(phin = rnorm(ns,mean=0,sd=1), alpha=rnorm(ns,mean=0,sd=1),/
>
> / mu = abs(rnorm(1,mean=0,sd=1)), sigma = runif(1,0,5),/
>
> / sigmaalpha = runif(1,0,5), delta = abs(rnorm(1,mean=0,sd=1)))}"/
>
> *5) * If I want truncated distribution, is it enough to just declare it in parameter declaration or should I put also
> eg. T[0,] behind sampling statement? Or both? Is there any difference? Isn't it useless to use T[] ?

Constraints in the parameter declarations leave the distribution
uniform over the constrained space. If the truncation is needed in
the log density, you need to include it. In general:

Foo(y|theta) T[L,H] = log Foo(y|theta) / (FooCDF(H|theta) - FooCDF(L|theta))

So if any of L, H or theta depends on a parameter, you need it.

- Bob
